Tedious and repetitive. You'll gradually descend into madness if you try to endure the repeated playthroughs. I thought it was clever the first few times, but it really wore on me. Although "things change", the gameplay is exactly the same every time.

It's a novel approach to a game, but get this on sale or not at all.

From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality.
How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe?
Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time!
The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made.
Is is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgements.
You are not beyond redemption.
You may change, and you may become more so much more than you were before.
If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe it is this...
What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience it leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world there is time for us to become our greatest selves as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.
It is literally every game ever created! It's Skyrim, it's Persona 3, it's all of them!

"This is the story of a man named Stanley.
Stanley worked for a company in a big building where he was Employee #427.
Employee #427's job was simple: he sat at his desk in Room 427 and he pushed buttons on a keyboard."
the single most iconic line in any game (mostly)

I like the new content personally, but I can see how some people feel it is repetitive if they've played the original. I think it is a good addition, the narrator seems slightly out of character at times, but it's not unbelievable. This is great to buy if you haven't played the original as it will feel like a full experience versus DLC, or add-on content, but I can see why they did this. I enjoyed the engine change to Unity, it looks better graphically, cleaner and crisp.
What a carefully crafted game. The only thing I think this game is missing is you pal. Just buy it and play it, then you'll probably love it if you're patient enough.

Stellar game-play. Very good commentary and meta commentary on gamer habits and difficulty of making games for the public. I enjoyed all the things that come with an art piece like The Stanley Parable.

Really short game that very cleverly utilizes the player's choice to extend the game for many hours. I'm pretty sure I didn't reveal each dialogue, each pathway, each outcome, but it was a fun time.

It did one thing that I was not fond of though... In order to 100% the game, you quite literally need to keep the game open for the entirety of a Tuesday. Never been a fan of "forcing" the player to just keep the game open. You also need to not play the game for 10 years and then open the game. Both can be completed by manipulating your PC's time, but I've never been a fan of such tactics. Still 100%d it though!
Buy this game and question everything. I am trying to get an achievement that takes me 10 years. Im not changing my clock. I have 10 years to spare.

I'd like to mention that the first version of the Stanley Parable is truly a masterpiece! Now, with the Ultra Deluxe version, this game has been elevated to a new level of excellence. The addition of new content and improved graphics seamlessly integrate with the already captivating gameplay, providing a fresh experience for both fans of the original and newcomers alike. The Ultra Deluxe version is an absolute must-play for anyone who seeks a thought-provoking journey into the nature of free will and choice.

The definitive way to play the Stanley Parable, everything from the original with added content and new endings.

10/10
Such a unique game and even replaying the game over and over again is entertaining!

The real 4th wall breaking was my system clock failing NTP synchronization and leaving me stranded 10 years in the future with expired certificates. 10/10, would break my system for a virtual icon again.

This is a silly/interesting game, I guess the best way to describe it(using my dad's words from telling him about it) is a "groundhog day" game. It's a little bit of insanity and a little bit of mess around and see what happens. It's a game were you can choose your own adventure in a sense by annoying the narrator and forcing him to change it by screwing around/doing something else.I've been messing around with this on the Steam Deck and didn't realize I had been going at it for 3 hours but that's just me cause I can easily get distracted if given the ability. It works great after messing around with the button layout(mostly to setup screenshots) though this mostly came from being new to the Steam Deck.

waiting 10 years to not play this game is the worst thing ever. im addicted to this game like a drug. i keep saying "just one more game before i attempt the 10 years..." but that never comes. i sit at my computer laughing and giggling like a little schoolgirl while this angry british man tells me im addicted to drugs and hookers. ever since the first game came out ive been a big fan, and i have never been more glad for a deluxe ever. i love this game so much, growing up with it shaped me as a person. this game is truly wonderful and i recommend it to anyone. best money i have ever spent. thank you for this game, truly it is wonderful and i cant describe it in any other way.
